title: Fire Fire Fire

timeline.title: GamePlay Details
bullets: In this puzzle game, players must skillfully stack a variety of objects to create a stable structure that allows fire to reach and burn the target.

Each level provides a set of items—such as wooden blocks, metal beams, and flammable objects—with different weights and properties. Players must drag and drop these items, balancing them carefully to prevent the stack from collapsing.
The challenge lies in ensuring the fire spreads to the target without burning out too quickly or missing the mark.

title: Murgen Horror

timeline.title: GamePlay Details
bullets: This multi-genre game allows players to explore haunted locations, uncover their stories, and defeat main ghosts. In each level, players begin by searching and solving puzzles to find the key to the room where the main ghost resides. Upon entering that room, players engage in combat mode with the ghost.

After defeating the boss, players receive items, clothes, and materials to equip themselves or enhance their camera. These items and equipment can also be purchased in the shop. The game features a blend of 3D third-person exploration, 2D puzzle-solving and searching, and 3D first-person shooter combat.

It is available on the Mirrativ app, which allows players to livestream their gameplay. Viewers can give gifts or gacha to players and chat with them. When there are viewers, players receive a strength boost at the beginning of the game.
Team composition includes a total of 18 individuals, with 8 working in the front-end team, 3 in the back-end team, 1 in project owner, 1 is director, 4 in design , and 1 serving as a tester.

title: Duplicate Folder

timeline.title: Features & Example
bullets: Preserves Variant Hierarchies: Ensures Prefab A Variant_copy points to Prefab A_copy instead of the original Prefab A.
Customizable extension filtering: Choose specific extensions to search and replace GUIDs.
Automatic same-hierarchy matching between Source and Target folders.

timeline.title: How to Use
timeline.subtitle: Tools/GUIDTools/Duplicate Folder
bullets: Source Folder: Select the folder to duplicate and copy its GUIDs.
Duplicate Folder: Create a copy of the folder in the same hierarchy.
Replace GUIDs: Specify the target folder, select extension checkboxes, and execute replacing to update GUIDs based on the matching hierarchy.

about: Duplicate Folder is a Unity Editor utility designed to facilitate the duplication of asset folder structures while correctly updating internal references (GUIDs).

When a Unity folder is normally duplicated, nested prefabs and variants may still reference the original folder's prefabs. This tool automatically relinks these references to point to the new duplicates in the same hierarchy.

title: Image Channel Packing

timeline.title: Features
bullets: Lossless packing: Pack up to 4 distinct grayscale pictures/masks into 1 texture.
Channel Selection: Choose which source channel (R, G, B, or A) to extract from each texture.
Invert Option: Option to invert channel values (1 - value) during the packing process.

timeline.title: How to Use
timeline.subtitle: Tools/Image Tools/Channel packing
bullets: Select your source textures for Red, Green, Blue, and Alpha slots.
Specify the source channel and toggle invert if necessary.
Click the pack button to generate the consolidated multi-channel texture.

about: Image Channel Packing is a custom Unity Editor tool that merges single color channels (Red, Green, Blue, or Alpha) from up to four different source textures into one packed texture.

This optimization technique is widely used in game development to store multiple grayscale masks (e.g., roughness, metallic, ambient occlusion, height) in a single RGBA texture, reducing draw calls and texture memory overhead.

title: Reference Hunter

timeline.title: Features
bullets: Bi-directional Reference Mapping: Easily list parent references (who uses this asset) and child references (what this asset uses).
Fast Cache System: Scans all assets in the project and stores cache indexes in a temporary directory for instant retrieval.
Automatic Selection: Auto-focus and highlight selected items in Unity's Project tab hierarchy.

timeline.title: How to Use
timeline.subtitle: Tools/GUIDTools/Reference Hunter
bullets: Click the Scan button to analyze files and cache the project's GUID reference graph.
Select any asset in your project hierarchy.
View parent and child assets in the Reference Hunter panels, click any reference to navigate to it.

about: Reference Hunter is a performance-oriented Unity Editor utility that parses asset files to map and display their dependencies (child references) and referencing files (parent references).

By maintaining a local scan cache, it provides quick lookups that help developer teams cleanup unused assets, trace prefab dependencies, and safely refactor directory structures without breaking references.

title: Socket Automation

timeline.title: Features
bullets: Socket & Mesh Panels: Automatic filtering and classification of bone sockets (SK_) and static meshes (SM_).
Visual Alignment: Toggle display of local rotation axes for precise alignment.
Parenting Automation: Parent SM_ meshes to SK_ sockets while maintaining relative/world transforms.
Automatic Naming: Auto-rename SM_ meshes with suffixes matching their target SK_ bones.
Export and Test: Batch export selected meshes and auto-assign random colored materials for quick previewing.

timeline.title: How to Use
timeline.subtitle: Script Execution
bullets: Run the Python automation script within your 3D application's script editor.
Select matching SK_ socket and SM_ mesh objects from the panel lists.
Click 'Parent Selected SM_ to SK_' or 'Setup Socket' to align and parent.
Use renaming/material controls to prepare the asset, then click 'Export select mesh'.

about: Socket Automation is a Python scripting utility designed for 3D modeling/rigging packages (like Maya or Blender) to automate the tedious process of setting up accessory sockets.

It separates and parses socket bones (with prefix 'SK_') and static accessory meshes (with prefix 'SM_'), allowing developers to parent, align pivots, auto-rename meshes, assign test materials, and batch-export FBX/obj files with one click.
